A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 17-page NI-Tex paper, including Appendices A and B. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of all sections, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original texture-generation experiments in Section 5, including KID/FID comparisons in Table 1, and baking-strategy PSNR results in Appendix B.4 and Figure 10.

after.justification: v3 retains the original texture-generation experiments, Table 1 KID/FID results, and Appendix B.4 baking-strategy PSNR results.

M1.justification: The dual-branch architecture, cross-pose and cross-topology augmentation, training losses, MR rectification, and uncertainty-guided iterative baking are identical in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both retain the same Objaverse, TexVerse, BEDLAM-derived training data, DeepFashion2 and 4D-Dress evaluations, and industrial/generated mesh scenarios. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Paint3D, Hyper3D OmniCraft Texture Generator, Hunyuan3D, and Meshy 6 Preview. The coverage-based baking comparator also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Training settings, preprocessing, sampling procedures, and evaluation metrics are unchanged, including the 10-object KID/FID comparison and Appendix B.4's 10-view baking evaluation using worst-view PSNR.

E4.justification: The view-selection comparisons in Figures 5 and 10 and the supplementary texture-consistency examples in Appendix B are identical. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report a fixed set of 42 random seeds for KID experiments in Section 5.3. No repeated-run information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. Table 1 retains NI-Tex's KID of 0.0364 and FID of 237.59, with identical comparator scores; Figure 10's PSNR results and all qualitative examples also match.

T1.justification: The problem definitions and Equations (1)–(9), including attention, losses, view selection, and texture reweighting, are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about non-isometric texture generation, the augmented garment dataset, and uncertainty-aware baking, with unchanged novelty and applicability claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including limited generalization to complex rigid deformations in Section 6 and the discussion of overfitting uniform MR properties in Appendix A.3.

D1.justification: Implementation details and release statements are identical, including eight H200 GPUs, approximately 10 training days, batch size 2, 512×512 resolution, and Appendix A's processing details. The code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 27 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to prior texture-generation and garment-generation methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 13 March 2026 to v3 dated 1 July 2026, with its hyperlink updated accordingly. All substantive wording, headings, and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–15, Table 1, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered content matches pixel-for-pixel outside the first-page version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The main text, experimental evidence, figures, and appendices are unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its hyperlink does not meaningfully alter scientific support, clarity, reproducibility, or overall paper quality.
